lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out consolidates the unit's vocabulary and grammar within a narrative context. Students listen to understand the story, then role-play the dialogue to practise fluency and intonation.
Look for attentive listening to the story, confident delivery of the dialogue during the role-play and appropriate use of expressions and gestures.
“Ben is joining our class today and Minh is showing him around. Let’s find out what she shows him.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers checks understanding of the key details from the story. Students read the questions and select the correct answers to show they followed the narrative.
Look for accurate recall of the story's main events demonstrated by the correct selection of answers for all three questions.
“Do you think Ben liked Minh’s art?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Read, write, and number

details: Read, write, and number strengthens narrative comprehension and literacy skills. Students determine the correct sequence of the story frames and complete the dialogue using context clues.
Look for correct logical sequencing of the story frames and accurate completion of the sentences using the words from the box.
“Ben’s brother has joined Lien’s class! He’s telling Ben about his first day, but has got a bit mixed up. Can you help order his story?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment

Homework Set:

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story allows students to personalize the narrative by choosing different subjects and activities. It encourages creative expression and provides communicative practice through role-play.
Look for logical choices in the story, neat writing and sticker placement, and enthusiastic role-play of the newly created dialogue with a partner.
“If you were showing a new kid your school, what class would you show them first? “

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Tongue twisters provide a fun and challenging focus on pronunciation. Students listen to and repeat the sentences, practising clear articulation of the target long vowel sounds (o_e and u_e).
Look for enthusiastic repetition and clear, accurate pronunciation of the target phonics sounds within the tongue twisters, even when said quickly.
“Great work showing the new kids around! Now let’s get them helping us with something really tricky - tongue twisters!”
